raw_case_text: Case 4: A 26 year old patient that reported exanthema and arthralgia in the second trimester of gestation. The qPCR was positive for Zika in serum (690 copies/ml) and the PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies. At 37 weeks of gestation, her baby boy was born by cesarean delivery that presented a cephalic circumference of 36.5 cm.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old pregnant woman presented with cutaneous exanthema and arthralgia during the second trimester of gestation.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: During the second trimester of pregnancy, the 26-year-old patient developed acute exanthema and arthralgia and was followed through delivery at 37 weeks of gestation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Pregnant woman in the second trimester of gestation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for exanthema and arthralgia during the second trimester.

objective.physical_examination: Exanthema noted in the second trimester. At 37 weeks of gestation, her male newborn delivered via cesarean section had a head (cephalic) circumference of 36.5 cm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Confirmed maternal Zika virus infection in the second trimester of pregnancy with term delivery of a normocephalic male infant at 37 weeks of gestation. Maternal ZIKV infection was confirmed by positive serum ZIKV quantitative RT-PCR (690 copies/mL) and positive 90% plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT90%) for neutralizing antibodies. She delivered a healthy baby boy via cesarean section at 37 weeks of gestation (head circumference 36.5 cm).
